description: Water chemistry models for the daily simulation. Candidate; scenario estimates, not validated.

records.name: Carbonate alkalinity buffer and pH (UQ-018)
records.summary: pH is solved each day from carbonate alkalinity and dissolved CO2 instead of a fixed drift per mg/L TAN. Alkalinity is a daily mass balance; dissolved CO2 is held at the level implied by the starting pH and alkalinity (aeration-controlled), because no CO2 transfer coefficient for raft or media beds was found.

equations.alkalinity_balance_mg_L_as_CaCO3_per_day: dAlk = - nitrification x TAN-N nitrified + denitrification_return x N denitrified + plant_nitrate_uptake_return x NO3-N taken up + water_exchange_fraction x (Alk_source - Alk) + base dose (as CaCO3)
equations.ph_solve: charge balance Alk = [HCO3-] + 2[CO3--] + [OH-] - [H+], with [HCO3-] = K1 CO2*/[H+] and [CO3--] = K2 [HCO3-]/[H+]; solved for [H+] by bisection; concentrations, no activity correction
equations.base_dose: if pH control and base dosing are on and pH is below target: alkalinity needed to reach the target at the held CO2, capped at max_dose_mg_L_as_CaCO3_per_day, split between bases by the scenario's base mix

nitrification_alkalinity_g_CaCO3_per_g_N.source: Ebeling, Timmons & Bisogni 2006, Aquaculture 257:346-358, doi:10.1016/j.aquaculture.2006.03.019, Eq. 14 (includes nitrifier growth)

review_metadata.confidence_reason: standard stoichiometry; the theoretical 7.14 (no biomass) from US EPA 625/4-73-004a differs by 1 percent

denitrification_alkalinity_return_g_CaCO.source: University of Hawaii CTAHR wastewater/aquaculture page (about 3.5 mg/L per mg/L NO3-N); standard US EPA nitrogen-control value 3.57 not read in full

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: extension page; the primary EPA manual was not fetched
review_metadata.confidence_reason: textbook stoichiometry, but only a secondary source was read

denitrified_share_of_residual_n_loss.unit: fraction of the calibrated residual N loss that is denitrification
denitrified_share_of_residual_n_loss.schema_choice_todo: Unknown. The residual N loss (nitrate_sinks) lumps denitrification and N leaving with solids. Default 0 is the conservative end (no alkalinity returned); 1.0 is the upper bound.

review_metadata.confidence_reason: gap: no source splits UVI residual loss into denitrification and solids N

plant_nitrate_uptake_alkalinity_return_e.unit: eq alkalinity released to water per mol NO3-N taken up (1 eq/mol = 3.57 g CaCO3 / g N)
plant_nitrate_uptake_alkalinity_return_e.source: Raven & Smith 1976, New Phytologist 76:415-431 ('almost one OH- per NO3-' assimilated, only part excreted by roots); Dickson & Fisher 2019, HortScience 54:1093-1100 (direction confirmed for basil and lettuce in hydroponics, per g dry weight)

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: direction is peer-reviewed; the released share in aquaponics is not measured
review_metadata.confidence_reason: the 0 to 1 band is a physical bound, not a measured aquaponics value

base_alkalinity_g_CaCO3_per_g.basis: computed from molar masses (50.04 g CaCO3 per eq / g base per eq); exact stoichiometry, not a measured value

carbonic_acid_constants.form: log K = A + B T + C / T + D log10 T + E / T^2 (T in kelvin)
carbonic_acid_constants.source: Plummer & Busenberg 1982, Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta 46:1011-1040, doi:10.1016/0016-7037(82)90056-4, as used in WATEQ4F/PHREEQC
carbonic_acid_constants.check: gives pK1 6.352 and pK2 10.329 at 25 C, matching Stumm & Morgan (6.35, 10.33) and WATEQ4F via the aqion compilation

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: coefficients were recalled, not read from a fetched page; the 25 C values were checked against a fetched compilation
review_metadata.confidence_reason: 25 C values corroborated; verify the coefficients against phreeqc.dat before accepting

water_ion_product_pKw_25C.note: used only in the charge balance; its effect at pH 6 to 8.5 is negligible

max_base_dose_mg_L_as_CaCO3_per_day.schema_choice_todo: No sourced cap. Practice guidance says add base slowly (UVI uses a separate base tank; SRAC 454). 30 mg/L/day is a model safeguard, not a sourced rate; it only binds in a large step correction.

fish_nh3_excretion_alkalinity_credit_g_C.basis: Charge balance: fish excrete most ammonia as NH3, which takes up an H+ when it becomes NH4+ (1 eq per mol N = 3.57 g CaCO3 per g N). If credited, net alkalinity use from excreted N that is nitrified is 7.05 - 3.57 = 3.48 g/g N.
fish_nh3_excretion_alkalinity_credit_g_C.schema_choice_todo: Modelling convention needs a decision. Default 0 applies Ebeling Eq. 14 to TAN as written (conservative, more base). 3.57 is the charge-balance credit; SRAC 452's RAS dosing rule (0.17-0.20 kg NaHCO3 per kg feed = 0.10-0.12 kg CaCO3-eq) matches the credited case (our arithmetic).

review_metadata.confidence_reason: inference from charge balance; no fetched source states the excretion credit

co2_treatment.basis: Dissolved CO2 is set from the starting pH and alkalinity and held. Aeration and fish respiration set CO2 within hours; no sourced CO2 transfer coefficient for raft or media beds was found, so a CO2 mass balance is not modelled. A scenario can give co2_mg_L directly instead.

reference_values.tilapia_co2_guideline_mg_L: below 20 (SRAC 452; Texas A&M); NRAES course operating limit about 60

calibration_check.uvi_observed_base_use: 40.65 kg Ca(OH)2 + 38.85 kg KOH per year (projected), 111.2 m3, pH 7.0-7.5, rainwater make-up 2.4 percent/day; Rakocy et al. ISTA6 (c. 2004), corroborated in order of magnitude by SRAC 454 (500-1,000 g doses several times a week)

uvi_derived_base_per_kg_feed_g.basis: our arithmetic from the ISTA6 doses and feed rate

calibration_check.note: Stoichiometric nitrification alone needs about 15 times more alkalinity than UVI adds. See the validation result for how the model compares.

limitations: No activity correction: pH may read about 0.05 to 0.1 low against course worked examples.
CO2 is held, so stripping, feeding peaks and night-time CO2 rise are not modelled.
Fish ammonia excretion is not credited separately; the 7.05 figure is applied to TAN nitrified.
Heterotrophic and algal assimilation are not modelled.
